sources.entry: Antville - Free, open source project aimed at the development of a high performance, feature rich weblog hosting software. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Javascript

summary.one_liner: Antville is an open source, feature-rich blog hosting software written in server-side JavaScript that can host many blogs on one installation.
summary.what_it_does: Antville is a multi-blog hosting platform built on the Helma Object Publisher, a Java-based JavaScript application server. The README says it can host tens of thousands of blogs, with server capacity as the main limit. It stores data in a relational database, and the README names PostgreSQL and MySQL as tested, with MariaDB expected to work. Antville can send notification e-mails if an SMTP server is configured. Helma includes an embedded Jetty web server, though the README notes another web server can be used instead. Helma maps HopObjects to database tables and builds URL paths that mirror the object hierarchy. The README also points to project, about, and help sites for documentation, and says the INSTALL.md file has setup instructions.
use_cases: host many blogs on one server
provide blogs for a community or organization
how_to_run: See INSTALL.md in the repository for detailed installation instructions
Set up a relational database such as PostgreSQL or MySQL/MariaDB
Configure an SMTP server if notification e-mails are needed
Start Helma with the Antville application (see INSTALL.md)
notable: Hosts tens of thousands of blogs on one installation, per the README
Written in server-side JavaScript on the Helma Object Publisher
Works with PostgreSQL and MySQL; MariaDB expected to work
Helma's URL structure mirrors its object hierarchy
caveats: The README says bugs may remain and the authors accept no responsibility for software behavior
Requires Helma Object Publisher and a relational database to be installed
Sending notification e-mails requires access to an SMTP server
